full_judgment: 2. The appellant is a Dealer in Jute and an income tax assessee. The Income Tax Officer of the appellant's circle issued a notice under section 22 (2) of the Income Tax Act on 26-7-51 for the assessment year 1951-52. Subsequent to the issue of the notice the appellant's case was transferred to the Special Circle, created under the Central Board of Revenues notification dated 24-8-51 whereupon a fresh notice dated 31 8-51 was issued to the appellant under section 21(2) of the Act by the Income Tax Officer of the Special Circle. The appellant filed a return on 20-10-51 for the accounting year ending on 31-3-51 and showed a total income of Rs. 3, 93,767/- Including the income from the jute business which started in and from 1950. The appellant raised an objection under section 5 and 64 of the Act praying for transfer of the case from the Special Circle but the said objection was overruled by an order dated 14-3-53 by the Income Tax Officer. The appellant was served with a notice dated 21-7-53 under section 22 (4) of the Act and was asked to file a fresh return to the accounting year sending on 30-6-51, as prescribed by the Central Board of Revenue under the notification dated 24-8-51 for those who started jute business after the 1st October, 1949. The appellant filed return under protest on 10-8-53 for the accounting year ending on 30-6-5 Land challenged the jurisdiction of the Central Board of Revenue and the Income Tax Officer to impose the special accounting year upon the appellant. The Income Tax Officer served a notice dated 10-8-53 on the appellant under section 23 (2) of the Act and passed his final order of assessment on 30 8 54 for the accounting year ending on 30-6-51.
